title: Frostbite
why: Architect Labs' AI agents design a new kind of CPU on their own, from its instruction set to the final chip layout, and in simulation it does 4.59 times as much work per watt as a modern in-order core; no chip has been made yet.

title: Smoktunowicz's gap theorem
why: Working alone for 94 minutes, GPT-6.2 Astra writes the first known computer-checked proof of a 2006 theorem by Agata Smoktunowicz about how fast certain algebras can grow, by a route of its own rather than the published one, Vals AI reports.

title: Navier–Stokes blowup
why: Working with Claude, Tristan Buckmaster and Levent Alpöge post a proof that the equations of fluid flow can break down even with no force pushing the fluid, the version of the Millennium Prize problem experts wanted; a data file the proof depends on isn't out yet.

title: Euler blowup
why: With AI help, Levent Alpöge, Tristan Buckmaster and Matei Coiculescu prove that an ideal fluid in a box whose sides wrap around can start spinning infinitely fast at a point in finite time, with every step checked in Lean.

title: McEliece challenges
why: MiniMax's unreleased internal model recovers the secret keys to 55 unsolved McEliece code-breaking challenges and makes the first practical breaks of several retired candidates for US encryption standards, MiniMax says.

title: Metal–organic frameworks
why: MOFGen, a team of AI agents built by Théo Jaffrelot Inizan, Kristin Persson and Omar Yaghi, designs new metal–organic frameworks, porous crystals that can capture carbon dioxide and pull water from air, and chemists make four of them in the lab.

title: MONAI Label zero-day
why: AI agents run by suspected China-linked hackers through the Cairn framework find an unknown flaw in MONAI Label, a medical imaging server, and use it to take full control of a university server, Amazon Threat Intelligence reports.

title: Masullo's GRH proof
why: Within hours of Ravi Vakil posting Alessandro Masullo's proposed proof of the generalized Riemann hypothesis, written without AI, several mathematicians report problems in it that they found with AI models.

title: Valiant's conjecture
why: An internal Claude model proves the algebraic version of P versus NP that Leslie Valiant posed in 1979, showing that the permanent of a matrix can't be computed efficiently with addition and multiplication alone; Lean accepts the 70-page proof, but no mathematician has checked it yet.
